findings.answer:
The window travels as one field of `Pins` from the profile TOML to the Ollama payload. Five hops.

1. The code default. `rota/llm/llm.py:40` sets `DEFAULT_NUM_CTX = int(os.environ.get("ROTA_NUM_CTX", "12288"))`. `rota/llm/llm.py:60` makes it the default of the `Pins.num_ctx` field.

2. The profile file. `rota/llm/profiles/local.toml:12` writes `num_ctx = 12288` under `[pins]`. `rota/llm/profile.py:34` lists `num_ctx` in `PIN_KEYS`, and `rota/llm/profile.py:74` copies it into `Profile.pins`. A second, per-role table exists: `rota/llm/profile.py:52` declares `context: dict` and `rota/llm/profile.py:75` parses `[context]`. Only one shipped profile uses it, `rota/llm/profiles/local-gemma-critic.toml:32-33` (`developer = 16384`).

3. The profile becomes Pins. `rota/llm/profile.py:156-164` `pins_for(role)` copies `self.pins`, then overrides with `self.context[role]` at `rota/llm/profile.py:159-160`, then builds `llm.Pins(model=model, **pins)`. The run's frozen profile is read back by `rota/llm/profile.py:273-279` `of_run(conn)` from the `profile` config key.

4. The run's drivers build the Pins. The cockpit night: `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1163` `_pins = (_prof.pins_for(None) if _prof else llm.Pins(...))`, handed to `loop_mod.run(pins=_pins)` at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1165-1168`. The walk: `probes/walk.py:122`. The CLI: `rota/cli.py:612`. Onboarding: `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:51`. Every one of them passes `None` as the role.

5. Per session, then the payload. `rota/core/loop.py:219` calls `run_session(conn, result.wake, backend=backend, pins=pins, ...)`. `rota/core/runner.py:1633` defaults it (`pins = pins or llm.Pins()`), and `rota/core/runner.py:1637` calls `routed_pins(conn, pins, wake)`. `routed_pins` at `rota/core/runner.py:103-131` is the only place the window can change per session: `rota/core/runner.py:125` reads `window = (prof.context or {}).get(wake.role)` and `rota/core/runner.py:131` writes `num_ctx=window if window else pins.num_ctx`. The pins then go to `backend.complete(system, user, pins, tools=schemas)` at `rota/core/runner.py:1810`. `rota/llm/llm.py:330-338` `OllamaBackend.options()` emits `"num_ctx": pins.num_ctx` at `rota/llm/llm.py:333`, and `rota/llm/llm.py:354` puts that dict under `"options"` in the JSON body posted to `/api/chat` at `rota/llm/llm.py:361-366`.

The LiteLLM provider is different. `rota/llm/llm.py:458-498` `LiteLLMBackend.kwargs()` never emits `num_ctx`. The docstring at `rota/llm/llm.py:441-446` says so: the pin stays as provenance only. So on `local-openai.toml` or `local-mixed.toml` the recorded 12288 is not sent to the server at all.

The object itself reaches the code that chooses the context size. The stored `wake_kind` and `wake_detail` are an output of the session, not an input to the sizing.

`Wake` is declared at `rota/core/scheduler.py:31-42` as a frozen dataclass with five fields: `role`, `kind`, `message_id`, `refs`, `detail` (`rota/core/scheduler.py:34-38`).

The path with no boundary on it: the scheduler builds the object (for example `rota/core/scheduler.py:112` for a message tip, `rota/core/predicates.py:707` for `tick:tests_missing`), `rota/core/loop.py:191` assigns it to `result.wake`, and `rota/core/loop.py:218-221` passes the object to `run_session`. `rota/core/runner.py:1611` takes it as the second positional parameter. `rota/core/runner.py:1637` hands the whole object to `routed_pins(conn, pins, wake)`. `routed_pins` is typed `wake: Wake` at `rota/core/runner.py:103`. Nothing is serialised and nothing is narrowed on that path. All five fields are live inside `routed_pins`.

`routed_pins` reads two of them. `rota/core/runner.py:111-112` reads `wake.kind` and `wake.role` for the routed model. `rota/core/runner.py:125` reads `wake.role` for the window. `message_id`, `refs` and `detail` are in hand and unused.

The boundary where the object stops is the return of `routed_pins`. From `rota/core/runner.py:1637` onward the window exists only as `pins.num_ctx`. `backend.complete(system, user, pins, tools=schemas)` at `rota/core/runner.py:1810` has no wake parameter. `OllamaBackend.complete` at `rota/llm/llm.py:341-342` and `OllamaBackend.options` at `rota/llm/llm.py:330` take only `Pins`. No name in `rota/llm/` is wake-shaped. So the `Wake` object never leaves `rota/core/`.

A second, softer narrowing happens at `rota/core/runner.py:1676-1685`: `sandbox_mod.build(..., wake=wake)` receives the whole object, but `rota/core/sandbox.py:465-468` keeps only `refs`, as `Ctx.wake_refs` (declared `rota/roles/api.py:66`). A role tool sees the refs and nothing else of the wake.

The stored columns are written at the end, after the sizing is over: `rota/core/runner.py:2350-2352` on commit, `rota/core/runner.py:2390-2391` on failure, into `sessions.wake_kind`, `sessions.wake_detail`, `sessions.wake_refs` at `rota/core/schema.sql:668-675` through `rota/core/db.py:540-550` and `rota/core/db.py:866-885`. Their readers are `rota/core/predicates.py:1041-1042`, `rota/core/scheduler.py:320-321` and `rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:463-487`. None of those sizes a prompt.

There are two sizing moments, and they know different things.

Moment one, the window. `rota/core/runner.py:1637`, `pins = routed_pins(conn, pins, wake)`. At this line the runner knows the whole `Wake` object: role, kind, message_id, refs, detail. It also has `conn`, `g` (`rota/core/runner.py:1631`), `backend` (`rota/core/runner.py:1632`), the incoming `pins` (`rota/core/runner.py:1633`), the derived `mode` (`rota/core/runner.py:1636`), and the caller's `batch_id`, `area`, `max_iterations`, `native_tools` (`rota/core/runner.py:1613-1620`). It does not yet know the prompt. `instructions` is composed after, at `rota/core/runner.py:1642-1646`. The sandbox is built after, at `rota/core/runner.py:1676`. `push_working_set` runs at `rota/core/runner.py:1720` and `build_prompt` at `rota/core/runner.py:1723`. So the window is fixed about 85 lines before a single character of the prompt exists, and nothing feeds the prompt's size back to it.

Moment two, the transcript budget. `rota/core/runner.py:1800`, `budget = _fit_budget(pins.num_ctx, len(system))`. Here the runner knows a great deal more: the full `system` string, the full `user` string (`rota/core/runner.py:1723-1724`), the `pushed` working set dict (`rota/core/runner.py:1720`), `inbound` (`rota/core/runner.py:1719`), the sandbox `sb`, the allowed functions (`rota/core/runner.py:1739`), the tool schemas (`rota/core/runner.py:1762`), `oneshot` (`rota/core/runner.py:1718`), and `wake` still whole. `_fit_budget` at `rota/core/runner.py:459-472` uses only two of them: `num_ctx` and `len(system)`. It returns `max(2000, int(num_ctx / 2 * 3.97) - system_chars)`.

The budget is applied at `rota/core/runner.py:1807`, `transcript = _fit(transcript, budget)`, inside the turn loop, so it runs on turn one as well. `_fit` at `rota/core/runner.py:475-529` cuts the wake block itself when the block alone exceeds two thirds of the budget (`rota/core/runner.py:502-506`), and evicts the middle otherwise.

No token count is ever taken. The runner measures characters and divides by 3.97, at `rota/core/runner.py:472` and again at `rota/llm/llm.py:415`. The only feedback about the real size arrives after the call, as `completion.truncated` (`rota/llm/llm.py:416`), reported at `rota/core/runner.py:1830-1838`.

All three exist in the code. Only the per-profile value is in effect on the night path today, and every shipped profile sets it to the same number.

The constant. `rota/llm/llm.py:40`, `DEFAULT_NUM_CTX = int(os.environ.get("ROTA_NUM_CTX", "12288"))`. This is the fallback when no profile is bound, through `Pins.num_ctx` at `rota/llm/llm.py:60` and the bare `llm.Pins()` at `rota/core/runner.py:1633`.

The per-profile value. `[pins] num_ctx` in the profile TOML. All eight shipped profiles set 12288: `rota/llm/profiles/local.toml:12`, `local-register.toml:14`, `local-openai.toml:15`, `local-openai-native.toml:14`, `local-mixed.toml:15`, `local-llama.toml:13`, `local-gemma-dev.toml:19`, `local-gemma-critic.toml:14`. It reaches Pins at `rota/llm/profile.py:157-164`.

The per-role value. Two code paths exist for it. The first is `rota/llm/profile.py:159-160`, inside `pins_for(role)`, pinned by `tests/rota/test_profile.py:177-178`. The second is `rota/core/runner.py:125`, inside `routed_pins`. Only one shipped profile carries a `[context]` table: `rota/llm/profiles/local-gemma-critic.toml:32-33`, `developer = 16384`.

There is no per-wake and no per-kind value. `routed_pins` reads `wake.kind` only for the model (`rota/core/runner.py:112`, through `rota/core/config.py:223-249`), never for the window. `rota/core/runner.py:125` keys the window on `wake.role` alone.

Observed, for grounding: nights 85 and 86 both bound the `local` profile with `pins = {'temperature': 0.0, 'num_ctx': 12288}` and an empty `context` table, and `SELECT DISTINCT num_ctx FROM sessions` returns the single row 12288 in each of `.rota/clickI_night85.db` and `.rota/clickI_night86.db`.

For the runner alone to read it, two files change. The object is already passed whole from the scheduler to `routed_pins`, so no plumbing is needed.

Minimum, two files:
1. `rota/core/scheduler.py:34-38` — add the field to the frozen dataclass. It must carry a default. 52 construction sites build `Wake` positionally or with a short keyword set, so a field without a default breaks all of them.
2. `rota/core/runner.py:103-131` — read `wake.<field>` inside `routed_pins`, beside the existing `wake.kind` and `wake.role`.

No change is needed in `rota/core/loop.py`. `rota/core/loop.py:218-221` already passes the object.

If the field must carry a real value rather than its default, every producer changes:
- `rota/core/predicates.py` — 30 construction sites, for example lines 211, 707, 828, 1109, 1902.
- `rota/core/scheduler.py` — 17 further sites, for example lines 112, 218, 293, 348, 468, 520.
- `rota/cockpit/progress.py:466`.
- `rota/testkit/fixtures.py:889` and `rota/testkit/fixtures.py:969` — the L1 and seam register paths.
- `probes/warm_stamp.py:75`.

If the field must be recorded on the session row, or replayed:
- `rota/core/schema.sql:668-675` — a new column beside `wake_kind`, `wake_detail`, `wake_refs`. There is no migration mechanism in the repository; `rota/cockpit/server.py:228` and `rota/cockpit/server.py:694-699` detect drift and refuse to serve a run that is behind `schema.sql`.
- `rota/core/db.py:284-286` — the `SessionResult` fields.
- `rota/core/db.py:540-550` — the commit insert.
- `rota/core/db.py:866-885` — `record_failure`.
- `rota/core/runner.py:2350-2352` and `rota/core/runner.py:2390-2391` — the two writers.
- `rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:463-487` — the reader.
- `probes/warm_stamp.py:68-75` — the only place a `Wake` is rebuilt from storage. It reconstructs from `role, wake_kind, trigger_msg, wake_detail, wake_refs`, so a sixth field is silently lost on a warm restamp unless a column carries it.

If a role tool must see it:
- `rota/core/sandbox.py:452` and `rota/core/sandbox.py:465-468` — `build()` already takes `wake=`, but only `refs` is copied into the Ctx.
- `rota/roles/api.py:66` — the `Ctx` field.

If the field changes the window, the cassette key changes too: `rota/llm/cassettes.py:118` hashes `pins.num_ctx` into the key, and `rota/llm/cassettes.py:41` stores it as a column.

surprises: The per-role window inside `Profile.pins_for` is dead on the night path. Every live caller passes `None` as the role: `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1163`, `probes/walk.py:122`, `rota/cli.py:612`, `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:51`. So the branch at `rota/llm/profile.py:159-160` never fires in a run, and the only reachable per-role window is the duplicate at `rota/core/runner.py:125`. Two implementations of one rule, one of them unreachable.

On the LiteLLM provider the window is never sent. `rota/llm/llm.py:458-498` builds the request and omits `num_ctx` on purpose (the docstring at `rota/llm/llm.py:441-446`). Four shipped profiles use that provider and still pin `num_ctx = 12288`, which is recorded as provenance only. Any plan that sizes a prompt against the recorded pin is wrong for those profiles.

The pushed working set is capped by a constant, not by the window. `PUSH_CHARS = 20000` at `rota/core/runner.py:409` and `SOURCE_CHARS = 14000` at `rota/core/runner.py:397` are fixed numbers. A 20000-character push is about 5000 tokens against the 6146 that survive an overflow of a 12288 window. Nothing scales those caps with `num_ctx`.

`_fit` is the only window-aware trim, and it runs after the window is chosen, on a prompt already built. `rota/core/runner.py:1800` computes the budget and `rota/core/runner.py:1807` applies it. There is no path that raises `num_ctx` because a prompt is large. The runner can only cut the prompt, never widen the window.

`routed_pins` swallows any failure of the profile load into a bare `except Exception` at `rota/core/runner.py:126-127`, which sets `think = None` and leaves `window` at `None`. A broken or unreadable profile therefore silently falls back to the caller's window, with no error line.

`num_ctx` is part of the cassette key (`rota/llm/cassettes.py:118`, column at `rota/llm/cassettes.py:41`). Changing the window per wake re-keys every recording for the wakes that change, so a per-wake window costs a re-record of the affected cases.

findings.answer:
Three readers, all in `rota/llm/discover.py`, and all reached through one entry point.

System RAM: `_ram_bytes()` at rota/llm/discover.py:160-183. It tries three sources in order: `psutil.virtual_memory().total` (discover.py:162-163), then on Windows `kernel32.GlobalMemoryStatusEx` through ctypes for `ullTotalPhys` (discover.py:166-179), then `os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE") * os.sysconf("SC_PHYS_PAGES")` (discover.py:180-183). It returns `None` when none answers. `psutil` is commented out of requirements.txt:25, so on this box the ctypes branch is the live one.

VRAM: `_vram_from_nvidia_smi()` at rota/llm/discover.py:202-212 shells `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.total,memory.used` and returns (total, free) in bytes. `_vram_from_ollama()` at rota/llm/discover.py:186-188 is a stub that returns `(None, None)` with the comment "Ollama reports no total".

Loaded-model bytes: `loaded()` at rota/llm/discover.py:191-199 reads `GET /api/ps` and returns `name -> (size, size_vram)`.

The single assembler is `system()` at rota/llm/discover.py:147-157. It calls `_ram_bytes()` (line 150), `_vram_from_ollama()` (152), falls back to `_vram_from_nvidia_smi()` (153-154), and on Apple Silicon sets VRAM total to RAM (151, 155-156). It returns a frozen `System` dataclass (discover.py:48-54).

`system()` has exactly one caller in the package: `setup.plan` at rota/llm/setup.py:50 (`machine = D.system()`). `loaded()` has one caller, rota/llm/setup.py:51.

The numbers are consumed in only two ways. (a) Fit arithmetic: `fit_of` compares need against `sys_.vram_total_bytes` then `sys_.ram_bytes` (rota/llm/discover.py:228-235) and returns one of `in_vram | spills | does_not_fit | unknown`. (b) Display: the TUI setup modal prints `ram_bytes >> 30` GiB and `vram_total_bytes >> 20` MiB at rota/cockpit/screens.py:640-643, and the cockpit server serialises the whole `System` into `/setup.json` at rota/cockpit/server.py:460.

Outside the package: `probes/bench/run.py:65-78` `gpu_fit()` parses `ollama ps` text for "100% GPU" or a "N%/M% CPU/GPU" split. That is a probe, not the run path.

No reader of RAM or VRAM exists anywhere in `rota/core/`. The run path never asks the machine anything.

Two separate things decide a model. A profile file picks it at onboarding. A routing string picks it per wake.

The profile file. `Profile` is a frozen dataclass at rota/llm/profile.py:41-67 with `default_model` (line 55) and `roles` (line 56). `Profile.from_dict` at rota/llm/profile.py:70-103 pops `models.default` into `default_model` (line 82) and keeps every other key of `[models]` as a role entry (line 83-84). The shipped files are in rota/llm/profiles/; `local.toml:14-19` is `default = "qwen3:8b"` with tester, critic, terminologist, developer on `qwen3.5:9b`. Lookup order is project `.rota/profiles`, then `~/.rota/profiles` (or `ROTA_HOME`), then the shipped directory: `places()` at rota/llm/profile.py:233-239, `find()` at 251-257. The default profile name is `ROTA_PROFILE` or `local` (rota/llm/profile.py:260-261).

Freezing. `cmd_onboard` finds the profile (rota/cli.py:471), runs `prof.check()` (472), and calls `profile_mod.bind` (477). `bind()` at rota/llm/profile.py:264-270 writes two config rows: `profile` as the whole dict (line 269) and `model_routing` as the derived string (line 270). `routing()` at rota/llm/profile.py:166-168 joins `role=model` pairs with commas. Both keys are declared settings at rota/core/config.py:167 and :172. `rota run --model/--role` rebinds the same way at rota/cli.py:529-530.

Per wake. `run_session` takes a base `pins` or `llm.Pins()` (rota/core/runner.py:1633) and immediately calls `routed_pins` (rota/core/runner.py:1637). `routed_pins` at rota/core/runner.py:103-131 calls `config_mod.routed_model(config.get(conn, "model_routing"), wake.kind, wake.role)` (lines 111-112). `routed_model` at rota/core/config.py:223-249 splits the string on commas, partitions each pair on the first `=`, tries a `role=model` pair first (lines 240-243), then a `tick=model` pair for a `tick:` wake (lines 244-248). A role pair wins over a tick pair (line 234 comment). The chosen model then keys the per-model `think` flag (rota/core/runner.py:117, 120) and the returned pins (rota/core/runner.py:130).

Where the base pins come from: `prof.pins_for(None)` at rota/tools/onboard_run.py:51 for a driven run, at rota/cockpit/tui.py:1163 for the TUI crank, and at rota/cli.py:612 for `rota profile toolcheck`. `pins_for` is rota/llm/profile.py:156-164.

The recommendation path is separate and advisory. `setup.plan` (rota/llm/setup.py:44-80) builds fit rows, then `D.recommend` (rota/llm/discover.py:239-265) ranks the benchmark table per capability group and takes the best-scoring model that is `in_vram`, else the best that `spills` (discover.py:256-263). `setup.choose` (rota/llm/setup.py:83-106) turns that into a default plus per-desk overrides. `setup.write` (rota/llm/setup.py:113-115) writes a user profile. Nothing in this path touches a running run; the profile file is the only product.

Today no function derives a window from memory. The arithmetic runs the other way: `num_ctx` is an input and bytes are the output.

The one function that joins a window to memory is `kv_cache_bytes(meta, num_ctx, bytes_per_value=2)` at rota/llm/discover.py:137-144. It returns `layers * heads * (klen + vlen) * num_ctx * 2` as an `int`, or `None` when the model metadata lacks `block_count` or `head_count_kv` (discover.py:142-143). It has one caller, `fit_of` (rota/llm/discover.py:222).

`fit_of(model, sys_, num_ctx, resident=1, loaded_bytes=None)` at rota/llm/discover.py:215-236 is where the machine facts meet the window. It returns a `Fit` dataclass (rota/llm/discover.py:57-65): `model`, `provider`, a `fit` string of `in_vram | spills | does_not_fit | unknown`, `weights_bytes`, `kv_bytes`, `need_bytes`, and `score` (always `None` from `fit_of` itself, filled later at discover.py:260). It returns a verdict about one window, never a window.

A cap that derived from RAM would have to be produced at `fit_of` or beside it in `rota/llm/discover.py`, because that is the only place holding both `System` and the model metadata. It would then have to reach the pins at one of two doors, and both are shut to machine facts today:

- `Profile.pins_for(role)` at rota/llm/profile.py:156-164. Returns `llm.Pins` (line 164). It reads `self.pins` and `self.context[role]` from the frozen profile dict only. All four callers pass `role=None` (rota/cli.py:612, rota/cockpit/tui.py:1163, rota/llm/profile.py:102, rota/tools/onboard_run.py:51), so its per-role branch at profile.py:159-160 never fires in a run.
- `routed_pins(conn, pins, wake)` at rota/core/runner.py:103-131. Returns `llm.Pins` (line 130-131). This is the live door: it is the only code that changes `num_ctx` per wake, and it reads the window from `prof.context` (runner.py:125), a dict out of the stored profile.

The third candidate is `setup.plan(driving=False, num_ctx=12288, table=None)` at rota/llm/setup.py:44-80. It returns a `Plan` (rota/llm/setup.py:35-41) carrying `providers`, `machine`, `rows`, `recommendation`, `groups`. It is the only function that already holds `D.system()` and every model's metadata at once, so it is the natural producer. Its `num_ctx` is a literal parameter default and neither caller passes one (rota/cockpit/tui.py:1006, rota/cockpit/server.py:455).

The consumer of any such cap would be the one place the window becomes a request: `OllamaBackend.options` at rota/llm/llm.py:330-339, which puts `pins.num_ctx` into the request body at line 333.

It is fixed at onboarding, with one per-role substitution applied at each wake from the same frozen profile. Nothing measures anything at run time.

The line that settles it is rota/core/runner.py:131:

    num_ctx=window if window else pins.num_ctx

That is the only assignment to `num_ctx` anywhere in `rota/core/`. `window` comes from rota/core/runner.py:125, `window = (prof.context or {}).get(wake.role) if prof else None`, where `prof` is `profile.of_run(conn)` (runner.py:119) reading the config row frozen by `bind` at onboarding. So the window is a table lookup by role, not a computation.

The chain of fixed values:
- `DEFAULT_NUM_CTX = int(os.environ.get("ROTA_NUM_CTX", "12288"))` at rota/llm/llm.py:43, read once at import, and the default of `Pins.num_ctx` at rota/llm/llm.py:60.
- `num_ctx` is a legal pin key at rota/llm/profile.py:34 and is read from `[pins]` at rota/llm/profile.py:74. Every shipped profile sets `num_ctx = 12288` (rota/llm/profiles/local.toml:12, local-mixed.toml:15, local-register.toml:14, local-gemma-critic.toml:14).
- `[context]` is parsed to `{role: int}` at rota/llm/profile.py:75 and held on the dataclass at rota/llm/profile.py:54. One shipped profile uses it: rota/llm/profiles/local-gemma-critic.toml:32-33, `developer = 16384`.
- `bind` writes the whole profile dict into config at rota/llm/profile.py:269, called from `cmd_onboard` at rota/cli.py:477.
- `pins_for` puts the role window into the pins at rota/llm/profile.py:160, but no caller passes a role, so that branch is dead in a run.

The only ways the number changes at all are out-of-band edits, not run-time adaptation: `profile.set_field` at rota/llm/profile.py:282-300 rebinds a new snapshot (`rota profile set <run> pins.num_ctx=...`), and `rota run --model/--role` rebinds at rota/cli.py:529-530 (models only, not the window).

The system detects overflow but never reacts to it. `OllamaBackend.complete` computes `truncated = used >= pins.num_ctx * 0.98 or estimate > pins.num_ctx` at rota/llm/llm.py:416. `run_session` reads that flag at rota/core/runner.py:1826 and only appends an error string naming the window (rota/core/runner.py:1833-1839). There is no retry, no widening, no re-send.     outcome.errors.append(
        f"prompt did not fit: {completion.prompt_tokens} of about "
        f"{whole} tokens evaluated against a {pins.num_ctx} "
        f"window — the server cut the prompt from the front, "
        f"which is where the brief is")
`whole` is `prompt_estimate` with `prompt_tokens` as the fallback, rota/core/runner.py:1831-1832.

That account reaches the database only if the session commits. `session_note(conn, session_id, outcome.errors)` at rota/core/runner.py:2376 writes the whole error list as one extra `turns` row whose completion text starts `SESSION ENDED. The runner's account:`, at rota/core/db.py:908-915. On a failure the list is not written by `session_note`; the except branch at rota/core/runner.py:2381-2397 writes a `session_fail` row carrying the exception only, so a truncation notice on a session that later dies is lost.

The only other consumer is `RunOutcome.errors` in memory, rota/core/runner.py:45. Nothing acts on `truncated`: the runner records it and continues the loop.

The LiteLLM backend is a separate path. `truncated` is never computed there, so a non-Ollama run never raises the flag.

Measured: _fit_budget(12288, 6000) = 18391 characters. So one pushed key at its cap already overflows the transcript budget before any second key, and the push cap cannot keep a prompt in the window.

The system prompt is never trimmed by anything. _fit_budget subtracts len(system) (rota/core/runner.py:472) but _fit only ever touches the transcript (rota/core/runner.py:488). If the brief plus the signature list grows past 22391 characters the budget floors at 2000 (rota/core/runner.py:472) and the wake is cut to 1333 characters, while the system prompt travels whole and ollama cuts it from the front.

_render_cut keeps the front and drops the tail (rota/core/runner.py:456-457), which is the opposite end from the one ollama drops. So when _fit trims an oversized wake it protects the wake line and the refs and kills the pushes, and when ollama trims the same prompt it kills the brief. The two cuts are not the same cut.

The runner takes no action on truncated. rota/core/runner.py:1825-1837 appends one sentence to outcome.errors and falls through. There is no re-fit, no retry, no window bump, and the turn's answer is used as if the seat had been briefed.

A truncation notice is lost when the session later fails. session_note runs only on the commit path at rota/core/runner.py:2376; the except branch at rota/core/runner.py:2381 writes session_fail with the exception only.
The truncated flag is computed only in the Ollama backend (rota/llm/llm.py:416). LiteLLMBackend (rota/llm/llm.py:438) never sets it, so any non-Ollama run is blind to a cut prompt.

The comment at rota/core/runner.py:401-403 says the pushes budget themselves at "code.area 14,000", but code_area's budget is 10000 (rota/roles/api.py:5969) and its own comment at rota/roles/api.py:5961 records that 14,000 was tried and reverted. The runner's note is stale.
The window is not one number. routed_pins can replace num_ctx per role from the run profile at rota/core/runner.py:124 and 131, so _fit_budget varies by seat within one night.

Twelve wake sites build `refs` whose length is a row count. Seven live in `rota/core/predicates.py`, three more in `rota/core/scheduler.py` behind a predicate that delegates to it, and one of those is the only capped one.

D:/repos/rota/rota/core/predicates.py

1. `awaiting_confirm` — `refs=tuple(r["id"] for r in rows)` at predicates.py:211-212. Query at predicates.py:199-202: `SELECT id FROM statements WHERE status = 'proposed' AND id NOT IN (SELECT value FROM config WHERE 0)`. The `NOT IN` subquery is a declared placeholder (comment, predicates.py:201) and `WHERE 0` returns no rows, so it excludes nothing. Counts: every statement in status `proposed`. Bounded by: nothing on the size. The guard at predicates.py:205-210 returns `[]` while an open `confirm` to the principal exists, which suppresses the wake but does not shorten it.

2. `contradiction` — `refs=tuple(r["id"] for r in rows)` at predicates.py:228. Query at predicates.py:220-221: `SELECT id FROM statements WHERE status = 'contradicted'`. Counts: every contradicted statement. Bounded by: nothing on the size. The guard at predicates.py:224-227 suppresses while an open `clarify` to the principal exists.

3. `term_collision` — `refs=tuple(ids)` at predicates.py:480-481, where `ids` is `r["ids"].split(",")` built at predicates.py:366-368. Counts: every live `glossary_terms` row in one stem group. See question 4.

4. `grouping` — `refs=tuple(r["tid"] for r in rows)` at predicates.py:532-533. Query at predicates.py:524-529. Counts: every distinct `criteria.ticket_id` not in a non-abandoned batch. See question 3.

5. `observed_entries`, the Liaison wake — `refs=tuple(offered)` at predicates.py:657-658. `offered` is built at predicates.py:579-587: the ids of every row with `basis = 'code'` in the four provenance views (`glossary_terms`, `constraints`, `model_areas`, `items`), minus ids already carried by a `present` message (predicates.py:570-573). Counts: the whole observed baseline. Bounded by: nothing. The docstring at predicates.py:549 says "Onboarding produces these by the hundred".

6. `observed_entries`, the two scheduler wakes — `refs=tuple(still)` at predicates.py:625 and `refs=tuple(fresh)` at predicates.py:644. `still` is built at predicates.py:637-643 (limbo rows still `code`-based and not ledgered); `fresh` at predicates.py:641-643 under the `lazy` election. Counts: the same baseline set, filtered. Bounded by: nothing.

7. `quarantined` — `refs=tuple(refs)` at predicates.py:1366. `refs` accumulates the `body_refs` of every message in status `quarantined` (predicates.py:1329-1337), then every id in a quarantined `tick_attempts` key that resolves to a batch, item or ticket (predicates.py:1344-1359). Counts: the payload ids of everything the run abandoned. Bounded by: de-duplication only (`if ref not in refs`, predicates.py:1336 and 1356). No cap.

8. `constraint_zero` — `refs=tuple(sorted(bound - want))` at predicates.py:1419-1420. `bound` is every grain bound to constraint zero (predicates.py:1408-1410); `want` is every area in `code_index` not yet surveyed (predicates.py:1414-1417). The routing rule is at `rota/core/loop.py:170`: `if wake.role in ("", SCHEDULER) or wake.kind.startswith("do:")`, the loop calls `_perform(conn, wake)` at loop.py:181 and returns. No model call. The comment at loop.py:162-169 states the three spellings of "not a role": the empty string, `SCHEDULER`, and the `do:` prefix.

So six of the nine unbounded ref sets become a model prompt. `observed_entries` is both kinds: it emits a scheduler wake under the `lazy` election (predicates.py:640-645) and a Liaison prompt otherwise (predicates.py:657-658).

The claim does not hold. `tick:grouping` is not bounded by work in flight, and nothing in the query or the predicate bounds it at all.

What the query returns (predicates.py:524-529):

    SELECT DISTINCT c.ticket_id AS tid FROM criteria c
    WHERE c.ticket_id NOT IN (SELECT bt.ticket_id FROM batch_tickets bt
                              JOIN batches b ON b.id = bt.batch_id
                              WHERE b.status != 'abandoned')

One row per distinct ticket that has at least one `criteria` row and sits in no batch whose status is anything but `abandoned`. It is a backlog query, not an in-flight query. The only thing that removes a ticket from it is a batch row, so a ticket enters the set the moment its first criterion is written and stays until the Architect groups it. `refs` is the entire result: predicates.py:532-533 takes every `tid`, and there is no `LIMIT`, no `ORDER BY`, and no guard that suppresses the wake while something is open — unlike `awaiting_confirm` (predicates.py:205-210), `contradiction` (predicates.py:224-227), `signoff` (scheduler.py:369-373) or `agenda` (scheduler.py:899-905). It re-fires every pass with the full remaining set.

Four things make it large.

1. Tickets accumulate faster than batches drain them. `tickets.slice` writes one row per slice (`rota/roles/api.py:3034`, staged at api.py:3033). `tick_criteria` (scheduler.py:280-294) fires per item for every ticket with no criteria, so each slicing session's whole output enters the set one criteria session later. Nothing pairs a slicing session with a grouping session.

2. One batch is one item's tickets, so one wake needs many sessions. `batches.group` refuses a set that traces to more than one item (api.py:3700-3711: "A batch delivers exactly one approved item"). If the set spans N items the Architect must run N times, and the first N-1 passes leave the rest of the set in the query, so the next wake carries it all again.

3. An abandoned batch gives its tickets back. `b.status != 'abandoned'` at predicates.py:528 is deliberate — the comment at predicates.py:517-523 records the S0 walk where a cancelled batch's tickets still "belonged" to it and nothing re-grouped them. `cancel` (predicates.py:1191-1214) abandons batches, so every cancellation returns its whole ticket set to this query.

4. Nothing ages rows out. A ticket whose item was never re-approved, or whose grouping session failed, sits in `criteria` forever and rides every later wake.

One thing that does shrink it: `DISTINCT` at predicates.py:525, so a ticket with five criteria counts once. The ref is the ticket id only, not the criterion text.

The claim is half right. One wake carries one word, but "the senses of one word" is not two — it is one glossary row per area that surveyed the word, plus the program-level row, plus any sense-tagged rows. The refs grow with the size of the tree.

How the set is built (predicates.py:357-368):

    groups: dict[str, list] = {}
    for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT id, term, area FROM glossary_terms WHERE superseded_by IS NULL"):
        groups.setdefault(_singular(_slug_of(r["term"])), []).append(r)

    rows = []
    for _stem, members in groups.items():
        if sum(1 for m in members if (m["area"] or "") != ".") < 2:
            continue
        rows.append({"term": members[0]["term"],
                     "ids": ",".join(sorted(m["id"] for m in members)),
                     "n": len(members)})

Every live glossary row is grouped by its stemmed slug. A group qualifies when two or more members have an area other than `.`. `refs` is then every member id of the group, `.`-area rows included — the comment at predicates.py:344-349 says so explicitly: "`.` stays out of the *count* while staying in the *refs*". The wake is `refs=tuple(ids)` at predicates.py:480-481.

What bounds one group. `glossary.amend` gives a second-and-later area its own id `slug#<area>` at `rota/roles/api.py:1570`, reached only when a prior row exists with a different area (api.py:1543-1569). So the family holds at most one row per area, plus the program-level row written by the define phase (area `""`, api.py:1576), plus any `slug#<sense_tag>` row from the `sense=` parameter (api.py:1447). The schema puts no unique constraint on `(term, area)` — `glossary_terms` is `id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` with a plain `term` and `area` (`rota/core/schema.sql:180-199`).

What makes it large.

1. The number of areas. `rota/onboarding/areas.py:31` sets `MIN_FILES = 3` and there is no cap on the count — `_area_count` at areas.py:290 just returns `len(set(proposal.areas.values()))`. A word that appears across many areas gets one row per area, which is the design intent recorded at schema.sql:186-189: "two written from different areas are the word doing different work in two places".

2. Plural and spelling variants that the id-merge misses. The kin-merge at api.py:1406-1413 only looks up `stem` and `stem + "s"` and skips any id containing `#`, while `term_collision` groups on `_singular(_slug_of(term))` (predicates.py:360). Rows written another way — the comment at predicates.py:325-330 names every fixture in the suite — carry ids that say nothing about the word and still join the stem group.

3. The number of wakes, not just their size. One wake per qualifying stem (predicates.py:476-481), so a glossary with many collided words produces many wakes, each with its own full family.

4. Nothing ages rows out. Only `superseded_by IS NULL` filters (predicates.py:359), and a row is superseded only by a disambiguation ruling. The `ruled` set (predicates.py:378-391) and the `raised` set (predicates.py:441-460) suppress the wake, they do not shorten it: the checks at predicates.py:476-479 are all-or-nothing over the group.

So the bound is the number of areas that use the word, not two. The `detail` field carries the word itself (predicates.py:481), which is one short string.

One does: `agenda`. It pages, and it is the only wake in either file that puts a `LIMIT` on its own refs.

`agenda` is declared at predicates.py:1370-1372 and delegates to `tick_agenda` (predicates.py:1386). The cap is at `rota/core/scheduler.py:915-919`:

    from .sandbox import PAGE_ASSUMPTIONS
    first = tuple(r["id"] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT id FROM ledger WHERE status = 'open' ORDER BY rowid LIMIT ?",
        (PAGE_ASSUMPTIONS,)))
    return [Wake("liaison", "tick:agenda", refs=first, detail=f"ledger={open_ledger}")]

`PAGE_ASSUMPTIONS = 7` at `rota/core/sandbox.py:32`. How it works, in four parts:

1. A hard `LIMIT` of seven ids, ordered by `rowid`, so the page is the oldest seven.
2. It is a page, not a drop. The full count rides in `detail` as `ledger={open_ledger}` (scheduler.py:919), counted at scheduler.py:907-909.
3. The next page comes on the next wake. The guard at scheduler.py:899-905 returns `[]` while a message to the principal is open, so presenting this page silences the tick until it is answered, and the answered rows leave `status = 'open'`, which advances the window. The docstring at scheduler.py:893-896 states this is what makes the tick terminate.
4. The same seven trims the pushed working set. `rota/core/runner.py:1472-1481` splits `ledger.list` into "this page" (rows whose id is in `wake.refs`) and a count line for the rest. The comment at runner.py:1470-1471 records the measurement: "51 open rows, 15,500 characters, pushed into a wake whose refs named seven". The same door-side rule is at sandbox.py:1077-1081.

Two near-misses that are not ref caps.

- `annotate` at predicates.py:753-758 has `LIMIT 1` in its query, and `batch_start` at scheduler.py:348 takes `ranked[0]`. Both cap the number of wakes; each wake already carries one ref, so neither pages a set.
- `outstanding` at predicates.py:1580 and predicates.py:1621 truncates with `[:8]`, but that function builds the register view, not a `Wake`. The truncation never reaches a prompt.

No other predicate caps, pages or truncates its refs. `runner.py:318-319` joins whatever arrives.

surprises: The attempt bound is keyed on the whole ref set, so it never bites on a growing one. `tick_key` at rota/core/scheduler.py:1333-1334 returns `f"{wake.role}|{wake.kind}|{','.join(wake.refs)}"`, and `note_dispatch` (scheduler.py:1337-1347) counts attempts against that exact string. For every unbounded predicate in question 1, adding or removing one ref produces a different key with `attempts = 1`. A `grouping` or `observed_entries` wake whose set changes between passes can therefore never reach the quarantine cap, while a stable set of the same size does. The key string also grows without limit, because `tick_attempts.tick_key` holds every joined ref.

`awaiting_confirm`'s query carries a dead filter. predicates.py:200-201 reads `AND id NOT IN (SELECT value FROM config WHERE 0)` with the comment `# placeholder join`. `WHERE 0` matches no rows, so the clause excludes nothing and every proposed statement is in the refs. If a de-duplication was intended here, it never ran.

`tests_missing` moves the unbounded list into `detail` instead of `refs`. predicates.py:707-709 sets `refs=(bid,)` but `detail="without a test: " + ", ".join(cids)`, where `cids` is every criterion of that batch with no test (predicates.py:705-706). `runner.py:339` appends `wake.detail` to the prompt body for every kind in `DETAIL_SHOWN`, so capping `refs` alone would not cap this wake's prompt contribution. `quarantined` does the same thing at predicates.py:1360-1364, building one `stalled` sentence per quarantined tick key.

`runner.py` already has two prompt-side trims keyed on `wake.refs`, for `tick:slicing` (runner.py:1458-1467) and `tick:agenda` (runner.py:1472-1481). Both shrink the pushed working set, not the `Refs:` line, and both exist because a measured night blew the window. The mechanism for "the wake names its subset, the push shows the rest as one line" is therefore already built and used twice, but is per-tick rather than general.

findings.answer:
Five surfaces exist. Nothing else reaches a person while a run is going.

**1. The live file, `.rota/live.md`.** `rota/llm/llm.py:150` reads `ROTA_LIVE`; `rota/llm/llm.py:170` defaults the target to `paths.REPO / ".rota" / "live.md"`. `LiveView` is at `rota/llm/llm.py:153`. It is opened at the head of every model call (`rota/llm/llm.py:367`), the header plus system prompt plus user prompt are written in mode `"w"` (`rota/llm/llm.py:175-180`), each streamed content chunk is appended by `token()` (`rota/llm/llm.py:192`, fed from `rota/llm/llm.py:266`), and `close()` appends `[done]` / `[timed out]` / `[unreachable: ...]` (`rota/llm/llm.py:205`, called at `rota/llm/llm.py:394`, `398`, `400`). `ROTA_LIVE=0` turns it off (`rota/llm/llm.py:165`).

**2. The cockpit web page.** Server at `rota/cockpit/server.py:322` (`do_GET`). The page is `rota/cockpit/viewer.html`; the logic is `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js`. It polls `/state.json` (`rota/cockpit/server.py:469`) from `refresh()` at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:549`, on a timer at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:847` — every 1.5 s while the `live` tab is up, every 6th second otherwise. The header carries a state pill (`rota/cockpit/viewer.html:368`) and a drift badge (`rota/cockpit/viewer.html:367`). The `live` tab (`rota/cockpit/viewer.html:421`) paints tips, predicates, sessions, receipts, messages, tool calls, items and counts (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:694-715`). A separate trace poll runs every 5 s (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:1020`).

**3. The TUI seat, `rota tui`.** `rota/cockpit/tui.py`. Its layout is at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:351-363`: a conversation pane, a `run_state` line, a `pulse` line (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:358`), the outstanding register, and a session ticker. `say()` mounts a chat bubble (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:424`). `note_step()` appends one line per session to the ticker (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:435`), fed by the `on_step` callback at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1144-1146`.

**4. The terminal, `rota run`.** `cmd_run` at `rota/cli.py:501` calls `drive` at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:41`. It prints one line per session at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:97-103`, an `idle:` line at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:105`, and the principal-language state at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:113` (`_say_where_we_are`, which prints `render_state`, `rota/roles/principal.py:183`).

**5. The terminal, `python -m rota.tools.talk`.** `rota/tools/talk.py:89` `_announce`, wired as `on_step` at `rota/tools/talk.py:136`. It prints the step line at `rota/tools/talk.py:98` **and up to four of the session's errors** at `rota/tools/talk.py:100-101`.

Two more things a person can read, but neither is live during a wake: `rota agenda` (`rota/cli.py:713-737`), a one-shot read of open asks; and `.rota/cockpit-<run>.log`, the cockpit server's own stdout when the TUI spawns it (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:882-888`).

Only one thing in the system holds a message until a person acts on it, and it is not one of the five display surfaces. It is a row in the `messages` table.

**The open message to the principal — the only dismissible surface.** `pending_asks` selects `status = 'open' AND to_role = 'principal' AND verb != 'converse'` (`rota/roles/principal.py:156-167`). The row stays open until the principal answers, and `land` closes it (`rota/roles/principal.py:598`, `616`, `727`). Approve, contest and defer are the dismissal. It is rendered in three places: `rota agenda` (`rota/cli.py:713-719`), the TUI (`show_ask`, `rota/cockpit/tui.py:454`), and the cockpit live grid's messages table (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:709`). The schema is at `rota/core/schema.sql:595`.

What each display surface does with a message today:

**The live file** destroys it. `LiveView.open` rewrites the whole file in mode `"w"` at the head of every model call (`rota/llm/llm.py:180`). A line written there survives until the next completion begins, which on a running system is under a minute. No dismissal state exists.

**The cockpit web page** derives everything and keeps nothing. `refresh()` overwrites each element from the `/state.json` snapshot on every poll (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:549`, `588-598`, `694-715`). A message is visible exactly as long as the condition that computes it stays true, and it vanishes the instant the condition clears. There is no dismissal store: `localStorage` holds only the selected view, the selected panel tab and the panel width (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:519`, `534`, `807`). The header badge and the state pill are the two elements that persist across tabs (`rota/cockpit/viewer.html:367-368`), because the pill is fed on every tab (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:842-847`).

**The TUI conversation pane** keeps a line for the life of the process. `say()` mounts a `ChatMessage` and never removes it (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:424-427`). It is unbounded and it scrolls away, but it is not overwritten. There is no acknowledgement and no clear.

**The TUI session ticker** trims. `SESSION_LINES = 30` (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:433`) and `note_step` removes the oldest children past that bound (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:441-443`). A line there is gone after thirty more sessions.

**The TUI pulse line** is one `Static` widget rewritten on every step (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:543`). It is the closest thing to a standing warning slot: it already colours yellow at three barren sessions (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:531`) and red past half the loop cap (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:541`). It holds while the condition holds, and nothing dismisses it.

**The terminal** scrolls. `print` with no state, at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:97` and `rota/tools/talk.py:98`.

**The TUI modal** blocks until answered — `ConfirmationModal` (`rota/cockpit/modals.py:20`) and `InputModal` (`rota/cockpit/modals.py:47`), both popped only by a button press (`rota/cockpit/modals.py:41`, `78`). It is used for destructive keys, not for status, and nothing in the runner can raise one.

Yes. Several, on four of the five surfaces.

**The one to name: the cockpit's `behind schema` header badge.** The text is set at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:592`. The element is `rota/cockpit/viewer.html:367`, styled amber at `rota/cockpit/viewer.html:30` with the `--warn` colour token from `rota/cockpit/viewer.html:19`. It is shown when `state.drift` is non-empty (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:590`), carries the missing pieces on hover (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:593`) and a reason line (`rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:596-597`). The data comes from `rota/cockpit/server.py:488-492`, which folds `schema_stale` into the drift list.

The others, for completeness:

Four paths exist today. Two are callbacks out to a surface, one is durable and goes through the database, one is the principal's message queue.

**Path A — `outcome.errors`, the runner's own account.** The runner appends a sentence to `outcome.errors` at fourteen sites (`rota/core/runner.py:1804`, `1833`, `1852`, `1875`, `1896`, `1913`, `1937`, `1971`, `1985`, `1999`, `2004`, `2116`, `2382`, `2396`). Exactly two things read the list.
  1. `session_note(conn, session_id, outcome.errors)` at `rota/core/runner.py:2376` writes them as one extra `turns` row headed `"SESSION ENDED. The runner's account:"` (`rota/core/db.py:910-914`). That row is durable and it is read by the cockpit session panel (`rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:201`, rendered at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:325-331`) and by the prompt panel (`rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:554`, rendered at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:1389`). It is not on any live surface — a person must click into that session.
  2. `Step.__str__` at `rota/core/loop.py:52` puts `errors[:1]` into the step line, **but only when the session did not commit**. A committed session with a warning prints `-> ok`.
  The one live reader of the whole list is `_announce` at `rota/tools/talk.py:100-101`, which prints up to four errors under the step line. It runs only under `python -m rota.tools.talk`, never under `rota run` and never in the TUI.

**Path B — `Step.note`, the loop's own account.** The field is `rota/core/loop.py:44`, set at `rota/core/loop.py:146`, `149`, `155`, `180`, `223` and `246`. `rota run` prints it in the session line at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:103` and as an `idle:` line at `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:105`. The TUI shows it through `str(step)` (`rota/core/loop.py:54`) in the ticker.

**Path C — the callbacks.** `loop.run` takes `on_step` and `on_completion` (`rota/core/loop.py:365-366`). `on_step(s)` fires once per session at `rota/core/loop.py:382-383`. `on_completion()` fires once per **model completion**, inside the runner's iteration loop, immediately after the turn is timed and appended (`rota/core/runner.py:1822-1824`). The TUI wires both: `on_step` at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1144-1146` into `note_step`, `on_completion` at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:1172-1173` into `_pause_for_single_step`. `on_completion` is the only existing hook that fires per turn rather than per session, and it already receives control at the exact point where a turn duration is known. Note that `rota run` does not use `loop.run` at all: `drive` calls `loop_mod.step` directly (`rota/tools/onboard_run.py:91`), so `on_step` never fires there.

**Path D — a row in `messages`.** The machinery outside a session can already change a message's fate: `quarantine_exhausted` (`rota/core/boot.py:167-186`) and `quarantine_looping` (`rota/core/scheduler.py:1395-1429`) both flip `status` to `'quarantined'`. Neither inserts a new message. The three non-test writers that insert one are `session_commit` (`rota/core/db.py:580`), the principal's own `land` (`rota/roles/principal.py:598`, `727`) and `talk.open_with` (`rota/tools/talk.py:80`). So no path exists today for the runner to raise a principal-facing message directly. A message written with `to_role = 'principal'`, `status = 'open'` and a verb other than `converse` would appear in `rota agenda`, in the TUI and in the cockpit messages table with no other change.

**The cockpit has no push channel.** The server opens the run read-only per request (`rota/cockpit/server.py:470`), computes `snapshot()` (`rota/cockpit/server.py:80`) and stats the db and `-wal` file for `quiet_secs` (`rota/cockpit/server.py:482-486`). Everything the page shows is derived from the database file plus its mtime. The runner reaches the cockpit only by writing a row.

**The column is `turns.ms`, at `rota/core/schema.sql:767`** — `ms INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, inside `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS turns` at `rota/core/schema.sql:761`. It is wall-clock milliseconds for one model round-trip.

**The writer is the runner's iteration loop.** `_started = time.perf_counter()` at `rota/core/runner.py:1809`, immediately before `backend.complete(...)` at `rota/core/runner.py:1810`, and the turn is appended at `rota/core/runner.py:1815-1816` as `Turn(iteration, system, user, completion.text, int((time.perf_counter() - _started) * 1000))`. The dataclass is `rota/core/db.py:261-271`, field `ms: int = 0` at `rota/core/db.py:271`. So the number covers the whole HTTP call: prompt evaluation, generation and stream consumption.

**It is persisted by three statements.** `session_commit` at `rota/core/db.py:613-616`, and `session_fail` at `rota/core/db.py:888-890` (kept turns) and `rota/core/db.py:892-894` (the synthetic `SESSION FAILED` row, always `ms = 0`). `session_note` also writes `ms = 0` at `rota/core/db.py:913-914`.

**It is read back in two places.** `inspect_api.session` at `rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:201-203` and `inspect_api.shown_to` at `rota/cockpit/inspect_api.py:554-556`. The page renders it as `"<n> ms"` beside each turn heading at `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:327` and `rota/cockpit/static/panels.js:1389`.

**Nothing else records a per-turn duration.** The `sessions` table (`rota/core/schema.sql:644-680`) has no time column. The only other duration is the wall-clock elapsed for the whole run, `time.time() - started`, printed once at quiescence (`rota/tools/onboard_run.py:56` and `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:66-67`). The cockpit's `quiet_secs` (`rota/cockpit/server.py:482-486`) is seconds since the db or `-wal` file was last written, not a turn duration. The Ollama backend does not keep the server's own `eval_duration` — only `prompt_eval_count` is read, at `rota/llm/llm.py:406`. `.rota-timings.json` (`rota/llm/cassettes.py:152`, saved at `rota/llm/cassettes.py:179-192`) times the test suite, not a run.

So a warning saying how slow a turn was has the number already, in-process, at `rota/core/runner.py:1816`, at the same point where `on_completion()` is called two lines later (`rota/core/runner.py:1823`).

surprises: The cut-prompt warning already exists and no live surface shows it. `rota/core/runner.py:1833-1837` appends the sentence to `outcome.errors`. For a committed session the list is read only by `session_note` (`rota/core/runner.py:2376`), which buries it in a `turns` row. `Step.__str__` shows `errors[:1]` only when the session did not commit (`rota/core/loop.py:52`), and a truncated prompt still commits. So on night 85 the runner knew and said nothing where anyone was looking.

`rota run` and the TUI drive the crank by two different routes, and only one of them can carry a callback. `rota/tools/onboard_run.py:91` calls `loop_mod.step` directly in its own for-loop, so `on_step` never fires under `rota run`. The TUI goes through `loop_mod.run` (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:1157`), which does fire it (`rota/core/loop.py:382`). A warning wired to `on_step` alone would be invisible to the night runs.

`python -m rota.tools.talk` is the only driver that prints `outcome.errors` live, at `rota/tools/talk.py:100-101`. It is the least-used of the three drivers. The two used every night print nothing from that list.

`turns.ms` (`rota/core/schema.sql:767`) is a duration column in a schema whose own header says at `rota/core/schema.sql:9-10` that "Time is not a concept: no dates, durations or deadlines appear anywhere in this file", and law 13 repeats it (`rota/LAWS.md:344`, `rota/LAWS.md:405`). The lint that enforces it, `tests/rota/test_schema_has_no_clock.py:12`, matches `_ms$` and so cannot see a column named bare `ms`. The allow-list at `tests/rota/test_schema_has_no_clock.py:11` names only `runtime_processes.started_at`. A turn-speed feature that leans on `turns.ms` is leaning on an unruled exception.

The TUI pulse line at `rota/cockpit/tui.py:502-543` is already a per-run warning slot with colour levels: yellow at three barren sessions (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:531`), red past half the loop cap (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:541`). It is rewritten whole on each step, so a second warning line costs one appended entry in the `bits` list.

`on_completion()` at `rota/core/runner.py:1823` fires once per model completion, two lines after the turn duration is computed, and the caller owns whether it blocks (`rota/core/runner.py:1817-1821`). It is the only per-turn hook in the system and today only the TUI's single-step pause uses it (`rota/cockpit/tui.py:1172`).
